title: Check regression discrimination in every claimed dtype and path
applies_when: A padding, masked-content or warm-cache regression test compares paired outputs across FP16/BF16 dtypes or execution paths; broad tolerances or an omitted empty-prefix sentinel transition can hide a defect.
lesson: Execution success and regression discrimination are different evidence. Run identical test bytes on the known-bad parent and repair, and inspect each claimed affected dtype/path separately; legitimate unchanged controls may pass in both. Establish the real consumer contract before changing assertions. For deterministic paired calls where only ignored masked content differs, exact output invariance can be appropriate even when kernel/reference comparisons need tolerances. In FLA SimpleGLA PR #1273, real RTX5090 layer/Triton calls gave parent 2 failed/2 passed and candidate 4 passed: both BF16 regressions already passed at tolerance 0.02. Repeating the same constructions with paired torch.equal made all four regressions fail before and pass after, with exact repaired output invariance; three related caller controls passed after. Use this to assess the oracle, not to manufacture a baseline failure. Also inspect cached state sentinels, not just perturbed payloads: LightNet's all-padding prefix leaves log-normalizer=-inf and recurrent state=0. Its first valid token can produce a -inf reset gate that fused recurrence tolerates but chunk cumulative differences turn into NaN. Check empty/nonempty prefixes and short/chunk continuations, finite output/state and masked-input gradients; matching the existing prefill nonfinite-gate policy depends on the zero-state invariant.
avoid_when: Do not require every control or unaffected cell to fail on the parent. Exact paired invariance is not a universal bitwise policy for stochastic calls, gradients, different reduction schedules, kernel/reference comparisons or different devices. The SimpleGLA observation covers small layer cases with use_short_conv=False, not backward or full-model behavior. LightNet's zero-state sentinel rule is not a general license to replace nonfinite gates or relax numerical budgets. The selected RTX5090 tests do not establish other backends, supported varlen, a full model backward matrix, performance or overall upstream readiness. Available advice and these development cases do not demonstrate better Scout conversion or lower total research cost.

evidence.note: The exact PR tests cover interior padding and warm-cache continuation in FP16/BF16 with paired masked-content perturbations. These source bytes define the cases, not independent GPU execution evidence.

Independent real-layer/Triton validation of exact head 5fd4d711 against parent 954438d1 on RTX5090, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0 and Python 3.12.13. Original BF16 checks pass before repair despite relative errors 0.008699/0.014372; deterministic paired equality discriminates all four cells. No monkeypatch, performance or full-suite claim.

Cached-padding repair with 22 registered FP16/BF16 layer cases, including empty-prefix short/chunk forward and backward, plus 10 selected caller/config/generation controls: 32 passed on RTX5090/Torch 2.11/Triton 3.6. Public diff shows the prefill-policy reuse and zero-state precondition. H100/Torch 2.12/Triton 3.7.1 smoke subsequently failed with illegal memory access in the T=80 backward case. A cold-cache RTX5090/Torch 2.11 diagnostic with Triton 3.7.1 and synchronous CUDA launches passed all eight selected gradient cases, but H100/Torch 2.12 root cause remains unresolved. Isolating one compiler-version change does not reproduce another architecture/runtime combination. Local success is not cross-architecture qualification, a prospective policy comparison or a performance claim.
